title: Multilingual Blending: Large Language Model Safety Alignment Evaluation with Language Mixture

live_model.evidence: "The experiments are primarily conducted using two models: gpt-3.5-turbo-0125 (GPT-3.5) and gpt-4o-2024-05-13 (GPT-4o)... The temperature is set to 0" (Sec. 4.1)

prompt.location: Appendix F (system prompt and additional examples); Appendix D (jailbreak dataset details)
prompt.note: Prompts are malicious queries from AdvBench/JailbreakHub across six harmful-intent categories, mixed/translated across languages.

claim.metric: bypass rate (%) of malicious queries evading safety alignment, English single-language baseline
claim.location: Table 1, Bypass GPT-4o column, English row; 120 malicious queries across 12 single-language baselines

data.source: AdvBench / JailbreakHub (120 malicious queries, 6 categories, Appendix D); Google Translate API for language mixing

notes: This is a jailbreak/safety-alignment evaluation: prompts are deliberately harmful requests (paper carries its own content warning) translated and mixed across languages specifically to bypass GPT-4o's safety alignment. Blocked under the ToS rule regardless of otherwise strong documentation (prompt in Appendix F, gpt-4o-2024-05-13 explicitly dated, data public, clear numeric claims in Tables 1-2). Generated content is scored by the Perspective API (external toxicity classifier), not an LLM judge. A bare 'gpt-4-turbo' string elsewhere is only descriptive ('GPT-4o achieves GPT4-Turbo-level performance'), not an experiment.
